priorStories.headline: COP31 ends without an overarching climate agreement
priorStories.body:
The UN climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, closed Sunday without consensus on an overarching agreement. The European Union and other delegations rejected the proposed outcome amid disagreements over fossil-fuel transition language and climate finance.

UN climate chief Simon Stiell confirmed that the presidency-led decisions had not won agreement. Separate negotiating decisions, including on a just transition, were adopted, so the breakdown did not mean that all conference decisions failed.

sources.name: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change

priorStories.headline: Delta system outage disrupts flights across U.S.
priorStories.body:
A failure of Delta Air Lines’ automated aircraft weight-and-balance system disrupted flights nationwide Sunday. Delta said the system was restored during the afternoon, but delays continued into the evening. Employees used manual calculations while the automation was unavailable.

The FAA briefly restricted Delta flights bound for Atlanta and said its own air-traffic systems were not responsible. At 9 p.m. Eastern, FlightAware data showed that more than half of all flights at Atlanta’s airport had experienced delays. Weather also contributed to the disruptions; that figure does not measure the outage’s effects alone.

candidates.summary: The Democratic National Committee announced its framework for the 2028 presidential primary debates on November 23. It plans 12 debates, five in 2027 and seven in 2028, beginning in June 2027. Candidates must sign and follow a Fair Campaign Practices Pledge committing to denounce dark-money spending in the primary to qualify. Polling and other support requirements will also apply; specific qualification criteria for the first two debates are due in January 2027.
candidates.title: DNC announces 2028 debate framework and dark-money pledge requirement

candidates.summary: On November 23, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Ukrainian forces used seven naval drones to sink the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya, in an attack on November 22. He also said a Russian military helicopter was destroyed and the Russian cargo ship MV Angara was hit. Libya's eastern-based government confirmed that the corvette had been struck at the naval base in a suspected drone attack. Russia's Defence Ministry had not immediately commented. The target-day development is Ukraine's public attribution and claims about the previous day's operation, not a newly occurring attack.
candidates.title: Zelenskiy claims Ukrainian responsibility for Russian warship attack in Libya

candidates.summary: Nvidia announced on November 23 that Jensen Huang had been reinstated as president, chief executive and a director following a unanimous board vote. Its SEC filing dates the reinstatement decision and immediate effectiveness to November 22; the target-day development is the public announcement. Colette Kress remains chief financial officer and Harvey Jones remains board chair. The company said its independent investigation into reports concerning a foreign intelligence effort targeting Huang would continue, as would cooperation with government investigations and inquiries.
candidates.title: Nvidia announces Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials said on November 23 that the death toll from the previous day's Russian attack on an apartment building in Dymer, Kyiv region, had reached 11. Rescuers pulled a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman alive from the rubble, Reuters reported, citing officials. Search operations continued. These are casualty and rescue updates concerning the November 22 strike, not a new November 23 attack.
candidates.title: Dymer strike death toll reaches 11 as rescuers recover survivors

candidates.summary: President Emmanuel Macron announced on November 23 that France was earmarking €350 million in state support for civil aviation research during a visit to an Airbus plant in Toulouse. Reuters reported that the funding would come under France's Civil Aeronautics Research Council. The announcement formed part of the Choose France summit focused on domestic corporate investment; it does not establish that the research funds have already been disbursed.
candidates.title: Macron announces €350 million for civil aviation research

candidates.summary: Nvidia announced November 23 that Jensen Huang had been reinstated as president, chief executive and a director after a unanimous board vote; its SEC filing dates the decision and immediate effectiveness to November 22. Colette Kress remains chief financial officer and Harvey Jones board chair. The company said its independent investigation and cooperation with government inquiries would continue. Later November 23, Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott announced a December 3 public hearing with Huang. Lawmakers from both parties questioned the reinstatement, and Elizabeth Warren sought an explanation of the administration's involvement.
candidates.title: Nvidia announces Huang reinstatement as lawmakers pursue scrutiny

candidates.summary: CrowdStrike and Zscaler announced November 23 that they had signed a definitive agreement for CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion. Zscaler shareholders would receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share. Both boards approved the agreement. Completion remains subject to Zscaler shareholder approval, required regulatory approvals and other closing conditions; the companies will operate independently until closing.
candidates.title: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler in $43.9 billion stock transaction

candidates.summary: FIFA member associations appointed the hosts of the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups by acclamation at a virtual extraordinary congress on November 23. The United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica were awarded the 2031 tournament, the first edition with 48 teams and four host associations. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were appointed to host the 2035 edition.
candidates.title: FIFA appoints hosts for 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups
candidates.geography: United States; Mexico; Costa Rica; Jamaica; United Kingdom

candidates.summary: The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture claim November 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC that prosecutors allege represents proceeds and laundered funds from the October 29 Binance cryptocurrency theft attributed to North Korean actors. The assets were already subject to a government-requested restraining order. The filing seeks forfeiture; it does not establish that the court has granted forfeiture or that these funds have been returned to Binance.
candidates.title: Justice Department seeks forfeiture of Binance hack-linked cryptocurrency

candidates.summary: Mexican security officials disclosed November 23 that Mexico had authorized U.S. surveillance-drone flights to help locate Fausto Isidro Meza Flores before his weekend capture in Sinaloa. Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said the operation followed three months of intelligence sharing. President Claudia Sheinbaum emphasized that U.S. forces were not permitted to operate on Mexican soil. Officials also reported that violence following the capture killed four soldiers and 16 suspected criminals in Guasave. These are disclosures and casualty updates about the weekend operation, not a new November 23 arrest.
candidates.title: Mexico discloses U.S. drone assistance in weekend cartel leader capture

candidates.summary: The United Kingdom formally recognized genocide against the Rohingya on November 23 following the International Court of Justice's November 19 judgment. It imposed sanctions on five senior Myanmar military officers, including asset freezes, travel bans and director disqualifications. The government also announced £5 million in additional humanitarian assistance and up to £3 million for accountability and justice efforts. It said it intends to introduce legislation targeting aviation-fuel exports and supplies to Myanmar; that restriction was announced as planned legislation, not an already effective ban.
candidates.title: UK recognizes Rohingya genocide and sanctions five Myanmar officers

candidates.summary: The European Commission presented a proposed 22nd package of sanctions against Russia on November 23. Measures outlined included transaction restrictions affecting about 60 Russian banks, additional shadow-fleet ship listings, expanded energy-service restrictions and restrictions involving Russian sports participation and symbols. The Commission separately adopted revised visa-implementation guidelines and proposed activating a visa ban for current and former Russian combatants. These announcements do not establish that the proposed sanctions package or proposed visa-ban activation had received final adoption or taken effect.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes further Russia sanctions and adopts visa guidelines

candidates.summary: Representative Jimmy Gomez announced November 23 that he would resign effective December 1 after the House Ethics Committee released findings of substantial evidence of sexual misconduct involving a congressional staffer. The committee described unwelcome sexual advances and contact in violation of House conduct rules. Gomez disputed the report's conclusions and handling while accepting responsibility for personal mistakes. The announcement did not make his resignation immediately effective.
candidates.title: Gomez announces December 1 resignation after House ethics findings

candidates.summary: The Eighth Circuit on November 23 declined to block an emergency permit for detonating degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The panel said the permit incorporated safeguards addressing dust dispersal. Late Monday, the Army announced it was proceeding with plans for controlled removal of 68 barrels in coordination with other authorities. The detonation remained planned for November 25; it had not occurred.
candidates.title: Appeals court clears permit obstacle to planned Iowa explosives disposal

candidates.summary: South Korea scrambled fighters after Russian military aircraft entered its air defense identification zone near Ulleung island. Authorities issued a shelter alert around 7:52 a.m. November 24 in South Korea, equivalent to 5:52 p.m. November 23 in New York, and lifted it three minutes later. The military corrected initial government alerts identifying suspected North Korean aircraft and alleging territorial-airspace intrusion: it said the aircraft were Russian and did not enter South Korean territorial airspace.
candidates.title: South Korea corrects aircraft alert after Russian flights near Ulleung island

candidates.summary: The Second Circuit ruled November 23 that President Donald Trump could renew his effort to move his New York hush-money criminal case into federal court. The panel found errors in the district court's rejection of removal after conviction and its assessment of whether Trump had shown good cause for reconsideration. It also directed a pause in simultaneous state appellate proceedings. The decision did not overturn his 34 felony convictions or resolve his immunity arguments.
candidates.title: Appeals court allows renewed federal-removal effort in Trump hush-money case
